comparison: regularized ERM vs Bayes risk; diagonal rate carries stated logarithmic factors.
statistical_method: minimization of Result 1 orders and comparison to Bayes fixed point.

statistical_method: distributional consequence of AMP fixed point; Figures 2,6,7 compare histograms.

comparison: Optimal logistic coefficient correlation is 95.65; H and gamma recovery are undefined for logistic by construction.
statistical_method: Replicate-level aggregate; no interval or hypothesis test reported.

claim: The repulsion prior changes latent identifiability metrics more than predictive accuracy.
value: At N=2000, lambda=0 to >0 changes AUC 74.69 to 75.00, Jaccard 0.542 to 0.565, effective edges/RF 1.992 to 1.874, and overlap/RF 0.097 to 0.082.
comparison: Table 7 repeats the direction at N=5000: AUC 74.51 to 74.63 and Jaccard 0.581 to 0.619.
statistical_method: Means in Tables 3 and 7; no significance test for structural metrics.

claim: BHPI has more stable rare-disease discrimination on UKB.
value: Figure 2 shows per-disease delta AUC relative to tuned logistic, stratified by prevalence; no single aggregate number is printed.
comparison: LGBM and Classifier Chains have long lower tails for rare diseases, while BHPI matches or exceeds the baseline in the displayed distributions.
statistical_method: Per-disease delta-AUC distribution over 100 random splits; aggregation denominator and intervals are not stated.
evidence_sections: Figure 2 / Predictive Stability in the Rare-Disease Regime

claim: BHPI has competitive UKB calibration.
value: ECE 0.005 and Brier 0.041.
comparison: Optimal logistic has ECE 0.001 and Brier 0.041; LGBM 0.021/0.043; RAkELd 0.006/0.042.
statistical_method: ECE and Brier aggregate over the 66-disease UKB evaluation; per-disease/sample denominator and uncertainty are not stated.

claim: The hypergraph representation has a rare-disease advantage over low-rank and clique alternatives.
value: BHPI mean delta AUC versus logistic is +1.2 for prevalence <2%, +0.2 for 2-5%, and +0.2 for >=5%.
comparison: Paired Wilcoxon p-values are 3e-5, 0.11, and 0.02; BFR and clique-expanded variants do not match the pattern.
statistical_method: Prevalence-stratified mean delta AUC with paired Wilcoxon p-values; correction for multiple comparisons is not described.

claim: High-PIP edges carry the predictive signal and low-PIP edges are near chance.
value: UKB high-PIP-only AUC is 68.7, 69.6, 71.6 versus full 68.9, 69.7, 71.6; simulation high-PIP-only is 75.6 versus full 75.7.
comparison: Low-PIP-only is 58.6, 55.0, 57.4 on UKB and 51.2 on simulation; random subset is higher than low-PIP but below full.
statistical_method: PIP-thresholded masked-model AUC; threshold is PIP > 0.5 and no independent refitting is reported.

claim: UKB posterior structure is sparse, overlapping, and risk-factor selective.
value: With E=60 candidates, posterior expected active hyperedges are 27.2 and 28 have PIP > 0.5; most hyperedges contain 2-12 diseases.
comparison: The figure contrasts localized membership PIPs and selective factor activation with dense latent-factor representations.
statistical_method: Posterior inclusion probabilities and thresholded structural summary; no external structural ground truth.

claim: Smoking and Dementia examples illustrate divergent and convergent pathway membership.
value: Smoking is shown in respiratory and ulcer pathways; Dementia appears in vascular-cognitive, geriatric frailty, and metabolic-neurodegenerative pathways.
comparison: These are qualitative pathway examples supported by PIPs, edge widths, and cited medical literature.
statistical_method: Qualitative case study; no case-level effect size or causal validation.

claim: CAVI gives structural PIP calibration and prediction close to full Gibbs MCMC in the reported simulation.
value: CAVI H overlap 0.850 plus or minus 0.054 and AUC 0.741 plus or minus 0.008; ECE values 0.087, 0.028, 0.050.
comparison: MCMC H overlap 0.885 plus or minus 0.068 and AUC 0.747 plus or minus 0.009; ECE values 0.081, 0.058, 0.039.
statistical_method: Mean plus or minus standard deviation over 50 replicates; PIP ECE for H, z, and gamma.

claim: Initialization-aligned structure is stable while exact labeled-edge identifiability is not guaranteed.
value: Initialization overlap is 0.905 plus or minus 0.062 in simulation and 0.875 plus or minus 0.044 on UKB; cross-replicate overlap is 0.81-0.83 and AUC standard deviation is 0.01.
comparison: Remaining differences involve borderline diseases with membership PIPs near 0.5; relabeling-stable quantities are used instead of unique edge labels.
statistical_method: Permutation-aligned overlap and predictive variability; selection uses highest validation performance.

claim: The method has a measurable structural-discovery cost but low reported inference latency.
value: UKB E=60 uses 27.8 GB and 73.7 minutes of training with inference below 0.1 ms; simulation runtime rises from 1.6/4.1 seconds at E=10 to 3.2/9.3 seconds at E=20 for N=2000/5000.
comparison: Logistic uses 3.74 GB and 5.82 minutes on UKB with inference below 0.1 ms.
statistical_method: Single reported hardware configurations; runtime table, not a statistical uncertainty estimate.

claim: Gemma float32 no-context patches produce perfect token matching on the reported generation comparison.
value: perfect token matching; token denominator not reported
comparison: full-context baseline vs recomputed no-context Θ′
statistical_method: per-token paired logit/distribution comparison; no uncertainty interval, test, or seed count
author_interpretation: confirms the hypothesis in float32
adverse_explanation: only a shared-history one-step comparison; not a free rollout test

claim: Stable update resolves the reported low-precision token mismatch in the described Gemma run.
value: bfloat16: 87.5% agreement; bfloat16 (Stable): 100%
comparison: base bfloat16 versus stable bfloat16 and float32
statistical_method: token-match percentage; denominator not reported
author_interpretation: small/zero denominator in Δm causes numerical sensitivity
adverse_explanation: does not quantify variability across prompts or runs

claim: The same matching construction is shown for an image context.
value: qualitative 'continues to work'; no aggregate count
comparison: image-context baseline versus patched no-context Gemma 3 4B
statistical_method: per-token line plots of L∞ difference and TVD
author_interpretation: universality across textual and image contexts
adverse_explanation: image source and number of images are unreported

claim: Falcon has perfect token matching even in base bfloat16 in the extended suite.

comparison: Falcon full-context versus no-context updates under bfloat16 and float32
statistical_method: aggregated distribution plots and token-match bars
author_interpretation: absence of post-normalization scaling makes updates more stable
adverse_explanation: one architecture cannot establish all mappings in Table 1

claim: Four added textual prompts retain near-zero float32 distribution differences.

comparison: five prompt settings in Figures 6–7

author_interpretation: robustness across textual domains

claim: Starting from only the final layer harms fidelity, while earlier starts reduce stable-update norm.

statistical_method: boxplots and token-match bars; denominator unspecified

claim: Scaling and stable variants show similar fidelity; stable has lower update norm.

comparison: naive, scaling, stable × bfloat16/float32
statistical_method: boxplots, outliers, and bars; no tests or confidence intervals

claim: TCEC improves SDXL W4A4 image fidelity relative to SVDQuant.

comparison: SVDQuant W4A4 on SDXL.
statistical_method: Aggregate point metrics; no uncertainty or test reported.

comparison: SVDQuant W4A4 on SDXL-Turbo.

claim: TCEC improves a PixArt W4A4 row and is presented as solver-compatible.

comparison: SVDQuant W4A4 on PixArt.

claim: TCEC improves selected OpenSora VBench dimensions at W8A8 and W4A8.

claim: TCEC's displayed latency overhead is below 0.5% for four listed models.

claim: The two-step approximation outperforms the full-window Eq. (10) in the appendix's SDXL comparison.
comparison: TCEC Eq. (13) versus TCEC Eq. (10) on SDXL.
statistical_method: Table point values; bit-width is not restated in the caption.

claim: At fewer than three inference steps, appendix results show smaller reported gains.

claim: TCEC outperforms QNCD in the appended CIFAR-10 W4A6 DDIM-100 comparison.
comparison: TCEC W4A6 versus QNCD W4A6.
statistical_method: Point metrics from 50,000 generated samples; no uncertainty reported.

claim: The synthetic decomposition excludes redundant X3 and constant X5 while assigning zero norm to irrelevant X4.
comparison: Known structural ground truth in the d=5 analytical case.
statistical_method: Deterministic component L2 norms; no repeated sampling reported.
author_interpretation: The selected basis does not contain X3 or X5 and Table 1 confirms X4 irrelevance.
adverse_explanation: Only one crafted dependency structure is tested.

claim: In independent categorical settings, the derived Shapley values closely agree with KernelSHAP.
value: Car 100×ISE entries range from 0.00 to 2.89; Nursery entries range from 0.0 to 4.4. Reported computation is 0.5 s for Car and 54 s for Nursery.
comparison: KernelSHAP with 200 background samples across every class and feature.
statistical_method: Integrated squared error over the full dataset; no uncertainty estimate.
author_interpretation: The framework recovers the SHAP interpretation in competitive time.
adverse_explanation: KernelSHAP itself is an approximation and ISE is not identically zero.

claim: Mushrooms main effects reconstruct a class probability and rank the domain-relevant features.
value: The paper reports R2≈1, MSE 10^-15, 0.3 s, and ANOVA importance X5=29.36%, X9=22.91%, X20=18.91%.
comparison: Observational TreeSHAP reports 24.17%, 18.45%, and 17.16% for the same three features.
statistical_method: Single reconstruction metrics and normalized global L1 norms; no interval.
author_interpretation: Both methods identify odor, Gill Color, and Spore Print Color as most important.
adverse_explanation: Evaluation is tied to an empirical support and a known-structure dataset.

claim: Low-rank approximation makes sparse high-dimensional explanations fast but leaves material reconstruction residuals.
value: Poker main-only relative MSE is 49% in 1.8 s versus 10% at rank 5,000 in 10 min; Connect-4 is 13% versus 7%; Dota2 is 6% versus 5%.
comparison: rmain against rhigh for Poker Hand, Connect-4, and Dota2 Results.
statistical_method: Point estimates of runtime, R2, MSE, and relative MSE.
author_interpretation: A trade-off exists between runtime and accuracy because greedy rank selection becomes a bottleneck.
adverse_explanation: High-fidelity reconstruction remains difficult at the stated scale.

claim: Poker Hand attribution emphasizes ranks more than suits and differs from attention rollout.
value: ANOVA assigns about 18.1–18.3% to card ranks and 1.6–2.3% to suits; attention rollout is about 13.1% and 6.9%, respectively.
comparison: ANOVA global L1 importance versus attention rollout.
statistical_method: Normalized attribution percentages; no uncertainty estimate.
author_interpretation: The method recovers the game’s rank-dominant structure.
adverse_explanation: The task has a strong known rule, limiting generality of this visual validation.

claim: MNIST reconstruction improves as rank increases under spatially constrained search.
value: Relative MSE decreases from 41% at rank 674 and 10 s to 12% at rank 10,000 and 15 min.
comparison: Main Effects, Low rank, Middle rank, and High rank runs for one MLP.
statistical_method: Single point reconstruction metrics.
author_interpretation: Spatial structure can substantially optimize the general algorithm.
adverse_explanation: Spatial pruning changes the candidate space and is not a generic greedy-search cost.

claim: The closed-form formulation has lower measured hierarchical-orthogonality error than TreeHFD in the stated synthetic comparison.
value: Closed-form errors span 1.54×10^-19 to 3.57×10^-16; TreeHFD spans 1.77×10^-4 to 8.59×10^-3 across d=2 to 10.
comparison: Closed-form ANOVA against TreeHFD after both are said to perfectly reconstruct a depth-2 XGBoost target.
statistical_method: Maximum absolute inner product between fA and any subset fB; point values.
author_interpretation: The construction enforces hierarchical orthogonality to machine precision.
adverse_explanation: The comparison is restricted to the assumptions under which TreeHFD is theoretically valid.

claim: Constructed hybrids implement the two target tasks at the final position.
value: qualitative; no numerical accuracy reported in Section 5.1
comparison: construction versus requested task behavior
statistical_method: implementation statement; no reported aggregate
adverse_explanation: The main text supplies no construction-run table.

claim: SSM-first hybrid learns Selective Copy at far smaller parameter count.
value: at about 2000 parameters: TF-TF 0.352, SSM-SSM 0.305, TF-SSM 0.433, SSM-TF 0.999
comparison: four layer-order architectures
statistical_method: accuracy curves; 11-run mean and p10/p90 bands described in E.1
adverse_explanation: Reverse hybrid does not separate from pure models.

claim: On Associative Recall with Decoding, only Hybrid reaches 0.5 at the tested scales.
value: caption says Hybrid reaches 0.5; pure models do not exceed 0.4
comparison: three-layer TF-TF, TF-SSM, SSM-SSM, SSM-TF
statistical_method: accuracy curves; percentile-band convention from E.1
adverse_explanation: Three layers are used because the construction needs them.

claim: Hybrid reaches high MKAR accuracy with fewer parameters.
value: SSM-TF 0.990 around 6000 and 0.989 around 12000; pure TF 0.668 around 12000
comparison: four architectures at matched sweep positions
statistical_method: accuracy curves and embedded values; percentile convention from E.1
adverse_explanation: Both hybrid and Transformer eventually perform at scale.

claim: Needle in a Haystack favors SSM-first hybrid and pure SSM over Transformer.
value: plot trends; caption gives no fixed value
comparison: four architectures under no context windowing
statistical_method: accuracy curves; percentile convention from E.1
adverse_explanation: The separation mechanism is left uncharacterized.

claim: Hybrid loses accuracy most slowly as evaluation length rises.
value: about 2 percent short-length separation grows to about 10 percent on longer sequences
comparison: Hybrid versus T_rope Transformer and Mamba
statistical_method: character-accuracy trajectories; no test stated
adverse_explanation: Only a synthetic task and stated model configuration are tested.

claim: Hybrid is best for almost all OOD train-bit proportions at test proportion 0.2.
value: Hybrid leads at 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.8; ties TF at 0.05; SSM leads at 0.9, 0.86 versus 0.80
comparison: SSM, TF, Hybrid across six train distributions
statistical_method: Table 1 point accuracies, no intervals displayed
adverse_explanation: Table 1 itself has no dispersion statistic.

claim: FlashSinkhorn reduces measured HBM traffic and runtime in the forward profiling setting.
value: At n=m=10,000,d=64,10 iterations: Flash 0.08 GB and 8.2 ms; KeOps 0.14 GB and 125.5 ms; Tensorized 98 GB and 54.0 ms.
comparison: Tensorized, KeOps, Flash on A100-80GB.
statistical_method: Single NCU profiling table; no interval or hypothesis test reported.
adverse_explanation: Working set fits L2; Table 5 says HBM traffic reflects L2-resident execution.

claim: Selected point-cloud forward and end-to-end benchmarks favor FlashSinkhorn over online baselines.
value: Table 3 reports forward 9.4–31.7x over KeOps and forward+backward up to 161x; JAX ratios reach 5.1x.
comparison: GeomLoss KeOps, GeomLoss Tensorized, OTT-JAX.
statistical_method: Mean timing across 50 forward and 30 backward repetitions; speedup is a ratio of timings; no variance/CI/test reported.
adverse_explanation: The selected table covers four n,d settings only; complete sweeps appear in Appendix H.

claim: The method retains linear measured memory scaling and reaches large HVP settings.
value: Figure 3 reports O(n) memory; at n=m=50,000,d=64 Flash HVP is 4.2s versus KeOps 14.5s.
comparison: FlashSinkhorn versus Tensorized, KeOps, and OTT-JAX.
statistical_method: Descriptive log-scale line plots and OOM/OOT outcomes; no uncertainty band.
adverse_explanation: The conclusion is measured on A100-80GB and fixed benchmark settings.

claim: The OTDD kernel supports label-augmented cost at n=60,000 without tensorized memory growth.
value: Peak memory remains under 1 GB at n=60,000; Tensorized OOMs beyond n=20,000 in the stated comparison.
comparison: FlashSinkhorn versus Tensorized baseline on MNIST to Fashion-MNIST.
statistical_method: Single dataset-pair scaling curves; no uncertainty expression.
adverse_explanation: KeOps lacks the custom discrete W lookup, so the labelled comparison is not a three-way baseline test.

claim: Streaming HVP enables an Adam-to-Newton saddle-escape protocol in the shuffled regression task.
value: Across 72 random initializations, Adam escaped 71; post-escape Newton median was 11 steps. Figure 5 gives 2423s versus 2785s for one trajectory.
comparison: Adam plus Newton versus Adam continuation/only.
statistical_method: Failure count, median, and single-run wall-time plot; no CI/test reported.
adverse_explanation: The data correspondence and transformation are synthetically generated and lambda_min thresholding is a protocol choice.

claim: The damped streaming HVP approximately matches a dense Moore–Penrose reference.
value: Default relative error is 4.24–4.89e-3 for epsilon 0.10–0.50; at epsilon 0.01 it is 8.54e-3 with 195 CG iterations.
comparison: Streaming damped Schur-CG HVP versus dense reference.
statistical_method: Relative Frobenius error for stated configurations; no repeated-sample uncertainty.
adverse_explanation: Damping causes a bias floor and low epsilon increases conditioning cost.

claim: Tensorized implementation can win at very high dimension while retaining a memory disadvantage.
value: Table 10 gives 0.5–0.7 Flash/Tensorized speedup at d=1024; Table 11 gives 0.5–0.9.
comparison: FlashSinkhorn versus GeomLoss Tensorized.
statistical_method: Fixed-setting timing grid; values below one favor Tensorized.
adverse_explanation: The paper attributes the reversal to on-the-fly recomputation at large d.

claim: Low epsilon preserves approximately constant per-iteration forward time but needs more convergence iterations.
value: At epsilon 0.10/0.05/0.01 Flash is 7.75/7.81/7.60 ms for ten iterations; convergence budget rises 2000/4000/5000.
comparison: Flash, KeOps, OTT-JAX; epsilon levels.
statistical_method: Descriptive timings and fixed precision comparison; no CI/test.
adverse_explanation: The total solve time grows because iteration budget grows, and HVP conditioning deteriorates.

claim: Extreme rectangularity reduces speedup but retains a large measured advantage in the tested grid.
value: Flash-over-KeOps is 13.3x at 10k by 10k and 8.3x at 500 by 50k.
comparison: FlashSinkhorn versus KeOps on rectangular pairs.
statistical_method: One A100 TF32 timing grid with ten iterations; no uncertainty expression.
adverse_explanation: Only about eight row blocks at n=500 limits parallelism.

claim: FlashSketch has a 1.73× global geomean speedup versus the next-best baseline over the listed RandNLA aggregate.
value: 1.73× global geomean; abstract rounds this to roughly 1.7×.
comparison: Table 1 aggregates shapes, datasets and configs over four RandNLA tasks against four dense/sparse baselines.
statistical_method: Geometric mean of speedups; the table does not specify configuration weights or an uncertainty interval.

claim: Primitive Gram/OSE speedups are largest against the FHT baseline in the aggregate table.
value: Gram: 2.67/4.17/16.22/7.64×; OSE: 2.69/4.16/16.20/7.63× versus cuSPARSE/GraSS/FHT/cuBLAS.
comparison: Dense Gaussian/cuBLAS, SJLT/cuSPARSE, SJLT/GraSS, and SRHT/FHT.
statistical_method: Task-level geomean speedups in Table 1; quality is separately plotted as error–time Pareto frontiers.

claim: End-to-end sketch-and-ridge and sketch-and-solve retain aggregate speedups.
value: Ridge: 1.42/1.54/3.94/3.10×; solve: 1.37/1.41/3.33/2.34× versus cuSPARSE/GraSS/FHT/cuBLAS.
comparison: Four baseline columns; residual quality is visualized against total wall-clock time in F.4–F.5 and G.3–G.4.
statistical_method: Geomean speedups in Table 1 plus configuration-level Pareto panels; no test or interval reported.

claim: Replacing only the GraSS projection kernel can reach about 3.2× speedup while retaining LDS on the plotted MNIST setting.
value: up to ∼3.2×; k=1024, 2048, 4096 after sketching from dimension 4k.
comparison: FlashSketch versus GraSS and three other projection baselines on an MLP trained on MNIST.
statistical_method: LDS is an average of per-example Spearman correlations over 50 retraining subsets; Figure 4 plots LDS against projection time per sample.

claim: Synthetic Stage I shows rapid outer-layer condensation while attention parameters stay high rank.
value: Qualitative Figure 2(A,B1); no numerical effect estimate is printed.
comparison: W0/W1 versus WQ/WK and initialized state
statistical_method: A displayed trajectory and heatmaps; no replicate, uncertainty, or hypothesis-test procedure reported.

claim: Synthetic Stage II aligns attention with a high-frequency-token focus.
value: Figure 2 caption identifies a synchronous increase between steps 350 and 550; no aggregate numerical summary.
comparison: first token versus all query pairs/other tokens
statistical_method: Time-series heatmaps and loss curves; no uncertainty expression.

claim: Synthetic Stage III retracts low-frequency embeddings and reduces their attention to the high-frequency token.
value: Qualitative Figure 2(B2,C,D); no effect size or run-level value.
comparison: token 0 versus low-frequency tokens before/after Stage III
statistical_method: Within-trajectory visual comparison; no error bar, interval, or test.

claim: Synthetic Stage IV opens directions orthogonal to the first token.
value: Figure 2(D3) displays a growing perpendicular-component norm; no replicate summary.
comparison: low-frequency W0[1:] relative to W0[0]⊥
statistical_method: Projection-norm time series; no uncertainty expression.

claim: The focus–dilution pattern repeats after Stage IV for later tokens.
value: Qualitative recurrence in Figure 2(D), expressed as a hypothesis.
comparison: token 1 and tokens 2–3 after token 0
statistical_method: Later-stage trajectory inspection; no additional controlled test.

claim: WikiText and TinyStories exhibit qualitatively similar focus, dilution, and retraction signatures.
value: Figure 3 gives selected-token/sample heatmaps and norm curves; no corpus-wide aggregate or effect size.
comparison: two real corpora and selected high/medium-frequency tokens
statistical_method: Selected trajectory visualization; no seeds, intervals, or tests reported.

claim: Early real-text behavior is presented as indirect support for a pseudo-2-gram Markov approximation.
value: Qualitative shift from uniform attention to self-attention; no direct non-Markov control comparison.
comparison: real text behavior against a Markov proxy interpretation
statistical_method: Interpretive observation, not a fitted or tested model comparison.

claim: 固定 prompt budget 下，可达性在临界长度附近快速下降。
value: Figure 2 的 sigmoid fits minimum R²=0.88。
comparison: PG19 与 random targets，memory lengths m=1,...,5。
statistical_method: 每个 (n,m) 是 20 targets 的 mean success rate，加 sigmoid fit；未报告 interval 或 seed variation。

claim: n50 随 memory length 的增长接近线性，且 natural-text targets 的 slope 大于 random targets。
value: R²_PG19=0.999；R²_random=0.995。
comparison: Qwen-2.5 1.5B 的 PG19 对 random strings。
statistical_method: n50 从 fitted sigmoid 的 0.5 crossing 取得，随后做 linear fit。

claim: support refinement 与 non-uniform cells 可缩小 theoretical-to-empirical slope ratio。
value: Table 1 Ball 7.77–20.4；Ellipsoid + Non-uniform Cells 4.56–10.82。
comparison: 七个模型、五种 support / precision strategy。
statistical_method: deterministic bound proxy 与 empirical slope 的 ratio；无 error bar。

claim: decoder-cell volumes 对多数模型高度不均匀，少数 token 占大量支持集。
value: Qwen-2.5 1.5B 最大空格 cell 为 0.81；Gemma-3 270M 最大 cell 为 1.1e-4。
comparison: Pythia、Qwen、Llama 和 Gemma 的 ranked decoder cells。
statistical_method: ellipsoid 内 N=50M uniform samples 的 token-frequency estimator。

claim: copying accuracy 在模型特异的长度阈值后骤降。
value: Figure 4 sigmoid fits 的 median R²=0.95；个别模型从 0.46 到 0.97。
comparison: 在 max length 50 训练后测试更长 unseen random strings。
statistical_method: exact-match accuracy 对 evaluation length 的 sigmoid fit；没有 replication uncertainty。

claim: support-bound estimates 随 maximum sampled prompt length 稳定。
value: Figure 9 caption 称 ell approximately 500 之后足以估计 upper bound。
comparison: Ball、Cone、Ellipsoid 与七个模型。
statistical_method: Monte Carlo support estimates 随 ell_max 作图；caption 未给 sampling interval。

claim: Random valid token splits can increase billed tokens while the fraction of plausible tokenizations falls as m grows.
value: Curves over 600 prompts; no single endpoint value is written in the main text.
comparison: Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, Ministral-8B-Instruct-2410, Gemma-3-1B-It; Algorithm 1 versus increasing m.
statistical_method: 5 repetitions and 90% confidence intervals in the plausibility panel.
author_interpretation: Longer random reports become less likely to be plausible, motivating transparency.
adverse_explanation: Algorithm 1 is not a transparent plausibility-preserving attack; the figure itself shows declining plausibility.

claim: Under Algorithm 2, a provider can overcharge users while reporting only plausible tokenizations.
value: For Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, up to 11.2%, 1.8%, and 0.28% at p=0.99, 0.95, and 0.90.
comparison: Truthful token count versus reported count under Algorithm 2 across three model families and p values.
statistical_method: 600 prompts, 5 repetitions, 90% confidence intervals.
author_interpretation: Revenue is unimodal in m because high m makes a candidate implausible.
adverse_explanation: The reported gain decreases sharply as p decreases and is conditional on successful plausibility.

claim: Algorithm 2 can increase average provider utility after the forward-pass verification cost.
value: For Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, gain exceeds 10.5% at p=0.99 and reaches 1.7% and 0.4% at p=0.95 and 0.90.
comparison: Algorithm 2 reporting policy versus truthful policy over provider profit-margin values.
statistical_method: Eq. (4), 600 prompts, 5 repetitions, 90% confidence intervals.
author_interpretation: Low-margin providers can benefit relatively more at high p.
adverse_explanation: The conclusion assumes the Appendix C.3 approximation for c_v and only covers specified model and sampling settings.

claim: An equal-price-per-character conversion preserves average provider margin in the presented sample while yielding some negative per-output margins.
value: For Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, 92.4%, 93.3%, and 94.1% of outputs have positive margin at rho_o 0.2, 0.4, and 0.6.
comparison: Pay-per-character per-output margin distributions at three old pay-per-token margins.
statistical_method: Empirical CDF over 600 multilingual prompts; dashed lines are empirical averages.
author_interpretation: The r_c = r_o*tpc prescription maintains the average margin as expected.
adverse_explanation: Outputs with lower-than-average characters per token, including non-English prompts, can be negative.

claim: Verification energy is approximately independent of output length under the measured execution configuration.
value: Llama-3.2-1B: c_o=2.642 +/- 0.004 J/token and c_v=15.188 +/- 0.005 J/output; five-model c_o/c_v range 0.174-0.509.
